parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Arti Bhagat (wife, seeking guardianship and custody)
parties.respondent_defendant: Deepak Kumar (husband, respondent in the petition)

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The applicant approached this Court seeking transfer of a petition under Sections 6 & 13 of the J&K Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act read with Section 25 of the Guardian and Wards Act, 1977 for guardianship as also custody of minor children. The applicant was harassed and had to leave her husband's house alongwith twin minor daughters and is living with her parents at Jammu.

legal_principles.principle: The power to transfer a case must be exercised with due care, caution and circumspection.
legal_principles.held: Although the discretionary power of transfer of cases cannot be imprisoned within a straitjacket of any castiron formula unanimously applicable to all situations, it cannot be gainsaid that the power to transfer a case must be exercised with due care, caution and circumspection.

legal_principles.principle: The convenience of the wife is to be given weightage for ordering transfer of proceedings at or near the place where she is residing.
legal_principles.held: Primarily convenience of the wife is to be given weightage for ordering transfer of proceedings at or near the place where she is residing.
cited_cases: Jatinder Kour vs. Sharan Pal Singh, (2016) 1 JKJ 670
Anju Bala vs. Narinder Kumar Bhagat, (2018) SCC Online J&K 533

legal_principles.principle: The principle is that the power to transfer a suit, appeal or other proceeding must be exercised with due care, caution and circumspection.
legal_principles.held: Above are some of the instances which are germane in considering the question of transfer of a suit, appeal or other proceedings. They are, however, illustrative in nature and by no means be treated as exhaustive.

legal_principles.principle: The principle is that the power to transfer a case must be exercised with due regard to the balance of convenience or inconvenience to plaintiff or defendant or witnesses.
legal_principles.held: Certain broad propositions as to what may constitute a ground for transfer have been laid down by Courts. They are balance of convenience or inconvenience to plaintiff or defendant or witnesses;

outcome.final_order: The petition for transfer was allowed, and the case was transferred from the court of Additional District Judge, Udhampur to the court of competent jurisdiction at Jammu.
